chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, from his father, from al-Asbagh, or from Habbah al-'Urani, who said:
Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام said upon the minbar of al-Kufah: “Whoever drinks a draught of khamr, then flog him; if he returns, then flog him; and if he returns, then kill him.”

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Title of Imam 'Ali عليه السلام, the Commander of the Faithful
key_terms.شَرْبَةَ خَمْرٍ: A drink or draught of wine/intoxicating beverage
key_terms.فَإِنْ عَادَ: If he returns to the act again
key_terms.فَاجْلِدُوهُ: Then flog him; a prescribed corporal punishment
key_terms.فَاقْتُلُوهُ: Then kill him; the stated punishment upon repeated recurrence
key_terms.مِنْبَرِ الْكُوفَةِ: The pulpit in Kufah from which the ruling was publicly proclaimed

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling in Shia hadith on repeated drinking of khamr?
ai.summary: This hadith records a legal ruling from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام concerning the punishment for drinking khamr. It establishes escalating penal consequences for repeated commission of the offense, reflecting the seriousness of intoxicants in Islamic law and public order.
